title: Topology-coalescer: hetero-aware prefill/decode scheduler and kernel ranker
creator: Aisha Kulkarni
description:
Background: We frequently see suboptimal kernel choices and degraded tail latency in mixed-workload clusters where GPUs are heterogeneously partitioned (MIG) or when a pool mixes H100/L40S/A10 nodes. Current heuristics pick kernels mainly by model/seq-length and single-GPU microbenchmarks, which fails under real cluster fragmentation, NVLink topologies, and dynamic clock/P-state shifts.

Goal: Implement a Topology-Coalescer component in the scheduler that: (1) aggregates current node topology, MIG slice layout, and recent clock/P-state telemetry; (2) scores candidate kernels by expected end-to-end tail latency and throughput for a given prefill/decode pattern; (3) influences route selection and prefilling placement so that small multi-slot sequences or bursty short/long mixes coalesce onto nodes and kernels that minimize cross-slice contention; (4) exposes a lightweight fallback path to conservative kernels when telemetry is stale.

Design summary:
- Topology snapshot layer: periodic (1s) aggregation of NVLink topology, MIG slice sizes/occupancy, GPU clock buckets, and recent per-kernel latency P50/P95. Low overhead: sampling of existing kernel telemetry + NVID statsd metrics.
- Kernel ranker: a small ML-free scoring function with tunable weights: (a) kernel throughput estimate from microbenchmarks, (b) slice contention penalty (based on MIG co-residency), (c) nvlink hop penalty for cross-GPU KV cache fetches, (d) clock uncertainty multiplier for nodes with variable clocks. Output: ranked candidate kernels per model variant.
- Prefill/decode coalescer: enum policy: {aggressive-coalesce, balanced, conservative}. Aggressive will batch small prefills onto fewer slices/kernels to reduce overhead; conservative spreads to reduce hot-spot risk. Default: balanced.
- Runtime integration: scheduler consults ranker when placing prefill jobs and picks placement that minimizes a combined score = kernel_score + topology_penalty + projected_queue_delay. When a placement would increase P95 beyond threshold, scheduler falls back to conservative kernel or routes to a different region.

Benchmarks (early lab runs):
- Mixed short(<=32)/long(>=1024) workload (70/30) on 4-node H100 pool with two nodes MIG-sliced: baseline P95: 128ms, throughput: 430 req/s. Topology-coalescer (balanced): P95: 106ms (-17%), throughput 506 req/s (+17%).
- H100/L40S mix with NVLink striping: baseline P95: 168ms, coalescer P95: 136ms (-19%), throughput +22%.
- Edge case: heavy fragmentation (many 1g.10g slices) saw small improvement (P95 -6%) but reduced variance.

Success criteria (measurable):
- P95 latency reduction >= 10% on mixed-size seq workloads in canary clusters compared to current scheduler.
- Throughput improvement >= 12% on balanced mixed workloads.
- No customer-facing errors due to scheduling misplacements during canary (<=0 incidents).
- Telemetry overhead <1% CPU and <1% network overhead in production hosts.

Tradeoffs and decisions:
- We avoid heavy ML models for ranking (explainability + low overhead) but keep model hooks for future learned rankers.
- Sampling interval of 1s chosen as a middle ground between reactivity and noise. If oscillation observed, will increase to 5s and add hysteresis.
- Aggressive coalescing risks hot spots; default set to balanced and can be toggled per-team.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge topology snapshot + ranker behind runtime flag (runtime.enableTopologyCoalescer).
2) Canary on internal perf cluster (canary-rt-02) for 72 hours, A/B against baseline.
3) Collect telemetry (P50/P95, cpu/mem, kernel choice distribution).
4) Gradual ramp to 10% production, 50%, 100% with 24-48 hour observation windows.

Observability and telemetry:
- New metrics: topology_coalescer.choice_ratio, topology_penalty_histogram, kernel_ranker_score_{kernel}.
- Dashboards: perf/runtime/topology-coalescer (canary vs baseline), and alert if choice_ratio changes >30% in 5m window.

Non-goals: automated kernel autotuning (future), rewriting kernel implementations, or modifying GPU clocks from the scheduler. This ticket focuses on placement and selection logic only.

Artifacts: Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/TopoCoalescerDesign. Bench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11823 (WIP).

Stakeholders: Runtime leads (Daniel Park), Serving infra (Lena Ortiz), Performance analytics (Ravi Singh), SRE (Hannah Lee).
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency on mixed seq workloads improved >= 10% in canary
No production incidents caused by scheduler placement during 7-day ramp
New telemetry emitted and dashboards created
Feature guarded by runtime.enableTopologyCoalescer flag and config policy per pool
steps: Prototype kernel ranker and scoring function
Integrate coalescer into prefill/decode scheduler with flag
Run lab benchmarks across H100/L40S/A10 pools
risks: Aggressive coalescing could create GPU hot-spots under unexpected traffic patterns
Telemetry staleness could cause bad placements; mitigated by fallback conservative kernel
Scoring function misweighting could prefer lower-throughput kernels in corner cases
Minor added CPU/network overhead for topology snapshots
next_steps: Finalize scoring weights and unit tests

Create canary dashboard and alert rules
Schedule 72h canary on canary-rt-02 with perf team monitoring
